rationale: All five newly paired maximum-label short-history comparisons fail, including artifact and sparse records with one prior episode; joint neural reading outperforms structured reading in every condition. Admit twelve frozen one-episode comparisons at 8192 labels, covering artifact, sparse and complete records under both shifts and both registered fits. These test training-budget dependence against the verified maximum-label outcomes and fill the same matched evidence comparison for the queued complete-record condition. The large direct-frequency losses and the absence of structured superiority must remain separate; no estimator, scoring threshold, lineage or fit setting changes. Same-fit native maximum-label references are already queued but unexecuted, so no native-to-shift contrast is claimed yet. Replenish measured useful work within the discovery ceiling, protected confirmation reserve and fixed cutoff, without occupancy padding.
